Hi Alex / Sanjay —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Nice to meet you both. Below is a short recap and the draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) milestone focused on POC environment setup so we can align on owners and timelines. I attached the MAP-v1.docx and the network diagram we discussed.

Recap (high level):
- Goal: 2-week POC to validate inference latency and cost for your map-routing workload on our Dedicated offering.
- Success criteria: 95th percentile latency < 200ms for 512-token inference, end-to-end cost within target range we discussed.

POC MAP milestone: POC environment setup (owner / dependencies / target date)
- Target complete: 2026-06-26
- Redwood owner: Marissa Cole / Nikhil Sharma (SE)
- Acme owner: Alex Johnson / Sanjay Mehta (Platform)
- Dependencies: VPC peering, IP allowlist, SSO/SAML test account, KMS/secrets access for API key provisioning, optional data subset for initial runs.
- Notes: We can use token-limited test keys until KMS is configured; final run will use customer-managed KMS.

Next steps:
1) Alex/Sanjay: confirm who will open the network ticket with your cloud team and share the peering contact + preferred IP ranges (ETA: 6/16).
2) Acme: share a SAML test user or IdP metadata (ETA: 6/17) so we can validate SSO for the Console.
3) Redwood: we will provision a temporary API key and send network IPs to add to allowlist once peering is scheduled (ETA: 6/15).
4) Procurement: we will share the MAP and draft SOW for signature after environment validation.

If the timelines above look tight we can slide the POC window by a week — let me know.

Thanks,
Marissa

Marissa / Rishi —

Quick notes from the SE side after reviewing Acme's reply and the diagram:
- Peering: we support GCP peering. For the Dedicated POC we typically stand up a temporary VPC in our cloud account and establish VPC peering to the customer project. That avoids exposing public IPs.
- IP ranges: we'll provide a small set of egress IPs for allowlist as a fallback, but peering is cleaner. I'll send the CIDR ranges and peering instructions by EOD.
- SSO: For POC, a SAML test user + local account is fine — we just need IdP metadata or a test user SAML assertion to validate the Console access.
- KMS/Secrets: For the POC we can use temporary Redwood-managed secrets if Acme prefers to delay KMS integration. For final validation we recommend customer-managed KMS; document that as a post-POC milestone in the MAP.

I'll draft the technical checklist and include the network/peering steps and a checklist for the Acme cloud team.

Thanks,
